explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/365, second question: 'Is the number of such n ≤ x [with n and n+1 both powerful] bounded by (log x)^{O(1)}?' The Lean statement asserts ∃ C > 0 and k ∈ ℕ such that, for all large x, #{n : 0 < n ≤ x, n and n+1 powerful} ≤ C·(log x)^k, which is the standard encoding of (log x)^{O(1)}. Excluding n = 0 (0 is vacuously powerful in Nat.Powerful) is correct and changes the count by at most one anyway. Faithful (positive form of the yes/no question).
